newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jobless rise proves Kohl failure - SPD's Lafontaine.
newsitem.headline: Jobless rise proves Kohl failure - SPD's Lafontaine.

text.p: Opposition Social Democrat (SPD) leader Oskar Lafontaine said on Thursday that the latest rise in German unemployment to a new post-war record showed that Chancellor Helmut Kohl's employment policies had failed.
"The further increase in unemployment shows that the policies of the Kohl government have failed. Germany needs new economic and finance policies," Lafontaine said in a statement.

"As an immediate measure the SPD demands a reduction in social security charges and tax cuts for workers and families," he added. The cuts are the key SPD demands in talks on tax reforms going on between the SPD and coalition government.
Lafontaine's statement was released before the publication of February unemployment figures, which were expected just before 0900 GMT.
But labour market sources said on Wednesday the February figures would show an unadjusted increase of 14,000 from the previous month to 4.672 million -- the highest since the 1930s.
Analysts said that the rise would translate into a seasonally-adjusted rise of up to 20,000 after the adjusted jobless figure surged by 160,000 to 4.317 million in January.
